text: The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because three key behaviors are pushing the default probability upward. First, the borrower has been late on payments in the 30‑to‑59‑day range twice; each late occurrence adds a strong positive weight to the risk score. Second, there is also one instance of a 60‑to‑89‑day late payment, which further raises the risk. Finally, the applicant is using about 59 % of their revolving credit limit, a level that the model associates with higher default likelihood. Together, these three factors contribute the most to the 87.7 % probability of default, leading the system to label the loan as high risk.
